user_id.description: The user the request is about, as a UUID.
user_id.name: user_id

task_id.description: The task the caller created for this step, which it then polls and whose result names the operation to perform. It is what makes the call idempotent: a retry resends the same id, so the server reuses that task rather than minting a new one and the durable workflow is sent only one message for it.

actuator-next-result.description: The result the durable workflow stores on an actuator/next task: what the actuator is to do next, and which workflow decided it. The actuator asks, performs what it is told, reports the result, and asks again, until it is told "done"; one run therefore performs as many operations against one transaction as the workflow needs, rather than the single operation the bundle's "type" used to bind it to.

dwork_id.description: The durable workflow that decided this operation, as a UUID string. Diagnostic only: the actuator logs it beside the operation so a run can be tied to the workflow that drove it, and acts on nothing else in it.

type.description: The operation to perform, and the discriminator of this protocol. "preview" plans the bundle and reports the plan. "commit" applies the saved plan that preview produced. "apply-auto-approve" applies a data-source-only bundle carrying no saved plan, so the workflow learns the current result of every data source before it decides what the preview must plan (RFD 584); it reports the applied state back with the same body "commit" does. "done" means the workflow has no further work, and is what ends the actuator's loop.

uploaded_files.description: The files the plan itself produced in the actuator's sandbox, one entry per capture target the actuator could read back. A data source writes at plan time, so a file it produces exists only for the duration of the plan and has to be carried out here; the server stages the entries in the transaction log and the commit that follows materializes them. Absent when the plan produced no such file, which is the ordinary case: a managed write-file resource writes at apply, so its target is legitimately missing during a plan.

task_id.description: The actuator/next task this result answers -- the id the actuator minted and sent to /actuator/next to ask for this operation. The server derives the durable-workflow idempotency token from it, so that two results delivered by one iterative run cannot collide: the index restarts at 0 for each operation, and a preview body and a commit body are the same variant to that derivation. It must come from the client because the client is what retries -- the same task id is resent on every attempt, so a retry dedupes and a new operation does not. Optional: an actuator that performs a single operation per run cannot collide, and one that omits it falls back to the older token.

admin-rights.description: Which administrative scope a user holds.  The backend stores one `admin` capability whose optional `tenants` allow-list is the scope; these two booleans are that single grant read apart, so at most one of them is true and both are false for a user holding no admin grant.

is_instance_admin.description: Whether the user's admin grant covers the whole installation -- an admin capability carrying no tenants allow-list, or one that permits every tenant (a "*" pattern with nothing negated). Both forms cover every tenant there is and every tenant there will be. False for a user whose admin grant only covers named tenants, which is_tenant_admin reports instead, and for a user with no admin grant at all.

is_tenant_admin.description: Whether the user administers named tenants rather than the installation -- an admin capability whose tenants allow-list permits something, but not everything. False for an installation-wide admin, which is_instance_admin reports instead; the two are never both true. Also false for a user with no admin grant, and for an admin capability whose allow-list permits no tenant at all.

window_start.description: Optional backfill start (YYYY-MM-DD). Omit for the steady-state trailing window.

blast-radius-edge.description: One dependency between two nodes, spelled in the direction the configuration is written in: the block at from_id DEPENDS ON the block at to_id. A change to to_id is what reaches from_id, so a renderer draws the arrow from to_id to from_id. Every edge here is one the subgraph walk's own guard admitted, so an edge the narrowing refused is absent rather than drawn and ignored.

attr_path.description: Attribute path the reading block names on the value, as separate segments, e.g. ["data", "name"] for local.content.data.name. Empty when the read names no attribute. Segments are kept apart because one can itself contain a dot.

from_id.description: id of the node that depends on the other. Always present in nodes.

kind.description: What the dependency is made of. "reads" is a reference to a value; "binds" is a module call filling a child variable; "reads_file" and "reads_tfvar" are a block reading a collected file or a tfvar. An explicit depends_on has no edge here: it orders an apply and carries no value, so a change does not travel along it.

to_id.description: id of the node that is depended on. Always present in nodes.

blast-radius-node.description: One HCL block in the blast-radius graph. Every block on a path from the queried block is a node, including a block that carries a dependency without being a resource -- a locals entry, a variable, an output, a module call, a data source -- so the graph shows the route a change actually takes instead of collapsing it. The node set is exactly the set the subgraph walk's expansion reached, so it is the same answer a plan would act on.

address.description: HCL address of the block, module-qualified and free of for_each / count index keys, e.g. "module.vpc.aws_subnet.private", "local.region".

id.description: Opaque identifier for this node, unique within the response. Edges reference nodes by it. Do not parse it; its construction is not part of the contract.

instance_addresses.description: State addresses of this block's instances, carrying their for_each / count index keys, in address order. Truncated to the first 50, so it can be shorter than instance_count. Empty for a block that has no state instances: a locals entry, a variable, an output, a module call, or a resource never applied.

instance_count.description: Total number of state instances this block has, never truncated. 0 for a block that has none.

is_seed.description: True for the one node that owns the queried instance. Exactly one node carries it whenever nodes is non-empty.

kind.description: HCL block type as written in the configuration: "resource", "data", "module", "variable", "output", "locals", "provider", "terraform", and so on. The empty string when the stored block carries no type.

module_address.description: Address of the module call this block is declared inside; the empty string for the root module.

resource_type.description: Terraform type of a resource or data block, e.g. "aws_instance". Absent for a block that has no type of its own, such as a locals entry or a module call.

state_id.description: State the block lives in. Can differ from the queried state, because a change crosses a terraform_remote_state boundary.

state_name.description: Display name of the block's state, for a graph that spans more than one.

kind.description: Which durable workflow minted this token: "preview" or "commit", the same string the workflow's own row records. The results endpoint routes a result on it. It rides here because it is fixed for the workflow's life, unlike the operation the actuator is performing, and reading it off the token spares a query per result message -- a large plan is delivered as many chunks. Optional: a token minted before this field existed carries no kind, and the endpoint then reads the workflow's row instead.

capabilities.description: Server capabilities: a single record of feature flags the UI uses to decide what to offer. Designed to grow: new capabilities are added as additional fields here rather than as new endpoints.

github_app_url.description: URL that starts the Stategraph GitHub App installation flow: GITHUB_APP_URL, or the page of the App the console created. Absent when neither exists, in which case the console offers to create the App, or tells the operator to install it from GitHub by hand.

cost-breakdown-entry.description: One row of a cost breakdown: a group -- a cloud provider, a Terraform resource type, or a tag value -- and the cost rolled up under it.

hourly_cost.description: Total hourly cost for the group, as a decimal string. Absent when nothing in the group is priced.

monthly_cost.description: Total monthly cost for the group, as a decimal string. Absent when nothing in the group is priced.

name.description: The group this row aggregates, e.g. "aws", "aws_instance", or a tag value. Tag-grouped rows use "untagged" for resources missing the tag key.

resource_count.description: Number of resources in the group.

cost-breakdown-entry-delta.description: One row of a current-vs-planned cost-breakdown delta -- a group (provider / type / tag value) with the cost on each side and the signed delta. Money fields and counts are absent on a side when the group doesn't appear there: an "added" group has no `current_*`, a "removed" group has no `planned_*`. Decimal-string deltas are signed ("+5.00", "-3.50", "0.00").

delta_monthly_cost.description: Signed decimal. Absent when neither side has a priced monthly cost.

delta_resource_count.description: Signed. Positive when resources were added to the group, negative when removed.

name.description: Group identity (provider name, resource type, tag value, etc.). Same conventions as cost-breakdown-entry.

cost-component.description: One billable line item contributing to a resource's cost. Mirrors the pricing-service schema; persisted verbatim into cost_snapshot_resources.components so the UI can render a breakdown without re-calling the pricing service.

hourly_cost.description: Decimal-string product of price x hourly_quantity. Omitted for monthly-only components.

monthly_cost.description: Decimal-string product of price x monthly_quantity. Omitted for hourly-only components.

name.description: Human-readable identifier shown in cost breakdowns.

price.description: Unit rate as a decimal string (preserves sub-cent precision; rates can carry ~10 decimal digits).

unit.description: Unit of measure for price and quantity (e.g. "hours", "GB-months").

costs-availability.description: Whether the server can meaningfully answer cost queries. Modelled as an object rather than a bare boolean so cost-related metadata can be added later without breaking the capabilities contract.

dedicated-availability.description: Whether the server offers dedicated-Stategraph provisioning (the "Create Dedicated Stategraph" flow and the personal/dev-eval tenant labeling). Modelled as an object rather than a bare boolean so dedicated-related metadata can be added later without breaking the capabilities contract.

gap-analysis-config-response-base.description: Base schema for gap analysis configuration responses

ready_for_gap_analysis.description: Whether the provider is ready for gap analysis

ready_for_terraform_import.description: Whether the provider has permissions for Terraform import generation

status.description: Configuration status (not_configured, partial, ready, error, not_implemented)

fetched_at.description: Unix timestamp when data was fetched from cloud provider

from_cache.description: True if this response came from cache

phantom_filtered.description: Count of provider default resources filtered out

github-app-availability.description: The orchestration GitHub App. configured: the engine has an App, from its environment or from the row the console created. ready: a running engine process holds that App, so it can be installed. An App from the environment is ready as soon as it is configured. creatable: this server can create an App from the console, which needs orchestration on, the engine's admin channel configured, and a self-hosted deployment. When it is false and no App is configured, the console asks the operator to bring their own.

github-app-credentials-request.description: Credentials the operator rotated on GitHub. GitHub shows each of them one time only and has no API that reads one back, so they are pasted here. At least one must be present; an absent one keeps its stored value.

app_id.description: The stored App's numeric id. The credentials are written only to that App, so a replacement made in the meantime cannot receive them.

client_secret.description: The OAuth client secret. The server signs in console users with it.

pem.description: The RSA private key, in PEM form.

webhook_secret.description: The secret GitHub signs webhook events with.

github-app-delete-request.description: Confirmation that the caller means to remove this App. The id must match the stored App's id, because removing it destroys the only copy of its private key.

github-app-manifest-request.description: What the console needs to send the operator to GitHub to create the orchestration App.

name.description: The App name. GitHub requires a name no other App uses.

organization.description: The GitHub organization that owns the App. Absent: the operator's own account.

rd.description: Console path to return to when GitHub sends the operator back. Rejected unless it is on this console, and it falls back to the getting-started page.

replace.description: The caller means to replace the App this server already has. Without it a server that has one refuses, so a stale tab cannot create a second App on GitHub by accident.

github-app-manifest-response.description: A form for GitHub's manifest flow: post manifest, as a form field of that name, to action_url. The state rides in action_url and comes back to the callback with GitHub's code.

manifest.description: The App manifest, as JSON text.

github-app-response.description: The GitHub App the orchestration engine uses. source is where it comes from: environment (the GITHUB_* variables, which win and hide any stored App), stored (created from the console) or none. app is present only for a stored App, since the environment's App is known to the operator who set it.

source.description: Where the App the engine uses comes from. environment: the GITHUB_* variables, which win and hide any stored App. stored: created from the console, and managed here. none: this server has no App. unknown: the server cannot read its own App, because it has no admin channel to the engine's database, so one may be in use.

github-app-stored.description: The App row, as the console may read it. The private key and the webhook secret are not readable.

app_id.description: GitHub's numeric id for the App.

created_at.description: When the App was stored, as an ISO 8601 instant in UTC with microseconds, for example 2026-09-29T07:12:08.123456Z.

html_url.description: The App's page on GitHub, where its settings and its keys are managed.

loaded.description: A running engine process holds this App. False right after a write, until the engine restarts on it.

slug.description: The App's name on GitHub, as it appears in its URL.

github-claim-request.description: A self-serve claim of a GitHub App installation for the tenant in the path, spending the proof cookie set by the claim callback.

installation_core_id.description: Stable uuid surrogate (terrateam's core_id) of the installation to link. It must be one the caller's proof names.

github-claimable-installations.description: The installations the caller's proof names that are still linked to no tenant. It is not paginated: the proof bounds the set.

results.description: The claimable installations, ordered by login.

github-unclaimed-installation.description: A GitHub App installation that no tenant has claimed yet. The instance admin's unclaimed listing and a tenant admin's claimable listing both return these. An instance admin links one with PUT /api/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/vcs-installations/{provider}/{installation_core_id}; a tenant admin who proved control of it claims it with POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/vcs-installations/github/claim.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp (UTC) when the orchestration side first recorded the installation.

installation_core_id.description: Stable uuid surrogate for the installation (terrateam's core_id), not the provider's bigint installation id. This is the id the link and claim endpoints take.

login.description: GitHub account the app is installed on: the organization or user login.

state.description: Installation state on the orchestration side, such as "installed", or "suspended" when the app is installed but suspended on GitHub. The unclaimed listing never includes installations removed from GitHub.

target_type.description: What the app is installed on: "Organization" or "User". A personal installation is otherwise indistinguishable from an organization one, since both carry only a login.

github-unclaimed-installations.description: One page of GitHub App installations that are still present on GitHub and linked to no tenant, newest first. Installations removed from GitHub are excluded: the orchestration side keeps their row forever, and claiming one would bind a tenant to an app that can never deliver anything.

has_more.description: Whether another page follows this one.

limit.description: The number of installations this page was allowed to carry.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, present only when has_more is set. Pass it back as the cursor query parameter.

results.description: The unclaimed installations in this page, newest first.

gitlab-provision-request.description: What it takes to provision a GitLab group as an orchestration installation: the group's id, its display name and a group access token.

access_token.description: GitLab group access token; write-only, never echoed back.

name.description: Display name of the GitLab group; stored trimmed.

gitlab-provision-response.description: A freshly provisioned GitLab group installation. The webhook secret is returned here exactly once, so the caller must store it.

installation_core_id.description: Stable uuid surrogate for the installation (terrateam's core_id), not the provider's bigint installation id.

name.description: Display name of the GitLab group, as stored.

state.description: Installation state on the orchestration side: "pending" right after provisioning, "installed" once the first webhook signed with the returned secret has arrived.

webhook_secret.description: Server-generated webhook secret, returned exactly once.

gitlab-rotate-request.description: Credentials to rotate on a GitLab group installation linked to the tenant: a new access token, a regenerated webhook secret, or both. At least one must be requested.

access_token.description: New GitLab group access token, stored trimmed; write-only, never echoed back. Absent leaves the current token in place.

regenerate_webhook_secret.description: When true, a new webhook secret is generated and returned exactly once. Absent means false.

gitlab-rotate-response.description: A GitLab group installation after credential rotation. The webhook secret is present only when regeneration was requested, and is returned here exactly once.

name.description: Display name of the GitLab group, as stored.

state.description: Installation state on the orchestration side, as stored: "pending" until a first webhook has arrived, "installed" afterwards. Rotation leaves it unchanged, so "installed" does not mean a webhook signed with a regenerated secret has arrived.

webhook_secret.description: Server-generated webhook secret, present only when regeneration was requested; returned exactly once.

instance-blast-radius.description: The blast radius of one resource instance, as a graph rather than a list: every HCL block a change to the queried instance would reach, and the dependencies that connect them. Nodes and edges both come from the subgraph walk that builds a plan, so this is what a plan seeded at this instance would act on. A client that wants each node's distance from the queried block computes it by walking edges out from root_id.

edges.description: Every dependency between two returned nodes. One entry per distinct pair and kind; an edge whose either end was dropped by max_depth is dropped with it.

nodes.description: The reached blocks, nearest the queried block first. Empty when the queried instance does not exist or its resource has no configuration block; otherwise it always holds the node flagged is_seed.

root_id.description: id of the node that owns the queried instance, so a client never has to recover it by matching addresses. The empty string when nodes is empty.

total_nodes.description: How many blocks the walk reached within max_depth, before the node limit cut the answer. Equal to the length of nodes when the limit did not bite, and greater than it when it did, so a client can say exactly how much it is not showing.

truncated.description: True when max_depth or the node limit dropped part of the answer, so the graph is a subgraph of the real one. A client must say so rather than present a partial graph as whole. Compare total_nodes against the length of nodes to tell which of the two cut it.

instance-cost.description: One row of a state-costs response: the latest priced result for a single resource instance, including its cost-component breakdown and the cloud metadata Stategraph extracted at snapshot time.

cloud_resource_id.description: Provider-native identifier (ARN, GCP self-link, etc.) when Stategraph could extract one from attributes.

components.description: Per-line-item breakdown that summed to monthly_cost / hourly_cost. Empty when supported=false or no_price=true.

hourly_cost.description: Estimated hourly cost for this resource. Decimal string (not a JSON number) so sub-cent precision is preserved. Absent when the resource is unsupported or unpriced.

monthly_cost.description: Estimated monthly cost for this resource. Decimal string (not a JSON number) so sub-cent precision is preserved. Absent when the resource is unsupported or unpriced.

no_price.description: True when the resource type is recognised but has no billable line items (free / unpriced type).

provider.description: Cloud provider inferred from the resource type (e.g. "aws", "google", "azurerm").

region.description: Region used for pricing (extracted from attributes, or falling back to the pricing default).

supported.description: True when the pricing engine has a builder for this resource type.

tags.description: Resource tags Stategraph extracted at snapshot time, for chargeback/grouping in the UI.

invitation-accept-request.description: Body of `POST /api/v1/invitations/accept`. Accepts the invitation named by the token, joining the signed-in user to the tenant. Acceptance happens after sign-in rather than during it, so all arrival cases -- already signed in, signed out with an account, or no account yet -- run the same server code.

token.description: The invitation token from the accept link.

invitation-accept-response.description: Result of accepting an invitation. Acceptance is idempotent for a user who was already a member, and the token -- not the session's email -- is the credential, so a mismatched address is recorded and reported rather than blocking the join.

already_member.description: True when the user was already a member before accepting; lets the UI say "you already had access" rather than implying the invitation granted it.

email_mismatch.description: True when the signed-in user's address differs from, or is absent for, the invited address. The join still succeeds -- the mismatch is recorded for audit and surfaced so the UI can interstitial it.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the user now belongs to.

tenant_name.description: The tenant's display name, for the confirmation the UI shows.

invitation-create-request.description: Body of `POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/invitations`. Invites one address to join the tenant.

email.description: Address to invite. Only lightly validated for an obvious typo -- the recipient's mail server is the real authority.

tenant_admin.description: When `true`, the invitee joins as a tenant administrator; when `false` or omitted, as a plain member.

invitation-create-response.description: Result of creating or reissuing an invitation. The invitation is returned together with a copyable accept link, so an administrator can pass the link on themselves even when email delivery is unavailable -- which is why a delivery failure does not fail the request.

delivery.description: How the invitation reached the recipient. `emailed` means the message was accepted for delivery. Every other value means nobody was emailed and the inviter must pass `invite_url` on themselves. Of those, only `transport_failed` is an actual fault: `not_configured`, `no_provider_key` and `inviter_has_no_email` are the supported link-only modes and must not be presented to the inviter as a delivery failure. The invitation is valid in every case.

invite_url.description: The accept link to give the invitee. Returned only here: only the token's hash is stored, so the link cannot be shown again -- reissue to mint a new one.

invitation-preview-response.description: The unauthenticated preview of an invitation, shown on the accept page before sign-in. The token is the credential, so no session is required, and the recipient address is masked so a forwarded or leaked link does not disclose who it was for.

invited_email_masked.description: The recipient address, masked (first character and domain kept) so the invitee can recognise it without the full address being disclosed to whoever holds the link.

inviter_name.description: Display name of the person who sent the invitation.

role.description: The role the invitee will receive: `member` or `admin`.

status.description: `pending`, `accepted`, `revoked`, or `expired`. The accept page uses this to decide whether to offer the accept action or explain why it is unavailable.

tenant_name.description: Name of the tenant the invitation grants access to.

required.description: Whether this edition of the server needs a license at all. The open-source edition does not, so 'false' means no license key is needed whatever 'licensed' says.

source.description: Where the license comes from, or 'none' when the instance has none. 'env' is a valid key from STATEGRAPH_LICENSE_KEY; 'stored' is a valid key entered at setup or under Settings > License.

default_limit.description: Row limit applied to a query that names no explicit LIMIT of its own. A query exceeding this without its own LIMIT is truncated and the response carries the mql-default-limit-applied header.

max_limit.description: Upper bound an explicit LIMIT is capped to.

orchestration-availability.description: Whether the server serves the orchestration integration (Terrateam fronted by Stategraph): the orchestration routes, the orchestration tables in MQL and the VCS login flow. Off when STATEGRAPH_ORCHESTRATION_ENABLED is unset. Modelled as an object like the other availabilities so orchestration metadata can be added later.

plan-operation.description: One resource-level operation from a transaction's plan: the instance address and what the plan will do to it.

address.description: The resource instance address the operation applies to, e.g. "aws_instance.web[0]".

operation.description: What the plan will do to the resource. A replace is one operation here, not a destroy+create pair.

plan-operations.description: One page of a transaction's per-resource plan operations.

results.description: Plan operations ordered by address. Paginated via Link header (RFC 5988): follow rel="next" for further rows. Empty when the transaction predates persistence or never planned (e.g. bulk-apply/import).

plan-summary.description: The "N to add, M to change, K to destroy" tally, aggregated from the persisted plan operations. A replace counts as both an add and a destroy, matching tofu's own tally. Absent on a transaction that never planned or predates operation persistence.

change.description: Resources the plan would update in place.

run-failure.description: A run that did not complete: the structured cause.

security-availability.description: Whether the server runs security scans: STATEGRAPH_SECURITY is "true" or "1". Modelled as an object so security-related metadata can be added later without breaking the capabilities contract.

security-finding.description: One security finding: the raw scanner record plus stategraph-derived enrichment. Identity within a state is by fingerprint = sha1(check_id || ':' || resource_fq_address); the same fingerprint persists across scans, so first_seen_scan_id / resolved_scan_id track the finding's lifecycle. The enrichment-derived fields blast_radius_resource_count, blast_radius_modules, is_internet_reachable, internet_reachability_evidence, and cross_state_refs are absent until the enrichment pass has populated them; workspace is also enrichment-derived but always present (joined from the owning state).

blast_radius_modules.description: Distinct module addresses touched by the blast (root module is the empty string). Pairs with blast_radius_resource_count: count is the quantitative scope, modules is the qualitative scope.

blast_radius_resource_count.description: Number of distinct resources reachable in the blast cone (transitive dependees), across all states. Populated by the enrichment pass; absent until enrichment has run.

cross_state_refs.description: State ids that reference this resource (cross-state dependency).

fingerprint.description: Stable identity across scans, hex sha1 digest.

first_seen_scan_id.description: Scan id at which this fingerprint first appeared for this state.

internet_reachability_evidence.description: Path through the graph plus confidence signal supporting is_internet_reachable. Schema deliberately loose; will tighten when the UI renders evidence.

is_internet_reachable.description: Whether stategraph's graph walk concludes this resource is internet-reachable. Populated by enrichment.

resolved_scan_id.description: Scan id at which this fingerprint stopped appearing. Absent while the finding is still open.

resource_fq_address.description: Fully-qualified resource address with module path, e.g. "module.web.aws_s3_bucket.logs".

severity_base.description: Severity reported by the scanner. Often absent (checkov frequently returns null severities).

severity_effective.description: Severity after context adjustment by the enrichment pass. One of "critical", "high", "medium", "low", or "unknown".

severity_reason.description: Human-readable explanation of why severity_effective differs from severity_base (e.g. "raised to critical: internet-reachable"). Absent when no adjustment applied.

source_file.description: User's source file path, translated from the reified-HCL path the scanner saw. Absent when no source location is recorded for the resource.

workspace.description: Owning workspace, joined from the state.

security-findings-summary.description: Severity breakdown and coverage summary for a state's latest current scan. Returned by GET /api/v1/states/{state_id}/security/findings/summary. 404 when the state has never been scanned to completion.

internet_reachable_count.description: Findings whose enrichment classified them as internet-reachable.

severity_breakdown.description: Per-severity finding counts. Missing keys default to 0.

top_checks.description: Top check_ids by failing count, most-impacting first.

security-scan.description: One scan envelope row: when a scan ran, by which scanner, in what mode, and how it concluded. Mirrors a row in `security_scans`.

kind.description: "current" = baseline scan of the state's HCL; "planned" = scan of a tx's reified subgraph (Phase 3).

scanned_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which the scan ran.

scanner.description: Scanner that produced the findings, e.g. "checkov". Schema is forward-compatible with future scanners ("mql", "drift").

severity_breakdown.description: Per-severity finding counts within this scan, e.g. {"critical": 2, "high": 5}.

status.description: "running" while the scan is in flight; "completed" or "failed" once done.

tx_id.description: Set only for planned scans (kind="planned"); absent for current scans.

security-scan-result-finding.description: One finding as produced by the server-side scan job ({!Sgs_security_job}), prior to enrichment / severity-derivation / lifecycle tracking. Identity is by fingerprint = sha1(check_id || ':' || resource_fq_address).

fingerprint.description: Stable identity across scans, hex sha1 digest computed as sha1(check_id || ':' || resource_fq_address).

resource_fq_address.description: Fully-qualified resource address with module path.

severity_base.description: Severity reported by the scanner. Often absent.

security-scans-response.description: Scan history for a state, newest-first. Paginated via Link header (RFC 5988); `total_count` is the unpaginated total of scan rows for this state.

security-state-findings.description: Latest current scan for a state plus its findings. Paginated via Link header (RFC 5988); follow `rel="next"` to fetch subsequent pages. `total_count` is the unpaginated total after the severity filter. When the state has never been scanned, `scan` is absent, `findings` is empty, and `total_count` is 0 -- security endpoints degrade cleanly (200, never 404).

mode.description: Operational mode of the server. Omitted in the default mode.

state-cost-actual-resource.description: Actual (FOCUS) spend attributed to one managed resource of the state: the billing lines whose cloud identifier matched it, summed over the loaded billing window. Billed fact, not an estimate; the window is this resource's own charge-period span.

address.description: Terraform address of the managed resource the billing lines matched.

billed_cost.description: Summed billed cost of the resource's attributed billing lines, decimal string.

currency.description: Billing currency when all of the resource's lines agree. Absent when mixed.

window_end.description: Latest charge period end (falling back to start) among the resource's attributed lines (RFC 3339).

window_start.description: Earliest charge period start among the resource's attributed lines (RFC 3339).

state-cost-actuals.description: Actual (FOCUS) spend attributed to a state's managed resources, summed over the loaded billing window: a state-level total plus the per-resource breakdown. Only attributed lines appear here -- unmanaged and unallocated spend are tenant-level concepts served by /costs/attribution and /costs/unmanaged. Empty resources + zero total when nothing has been attributed to the state.

billed_cost.description: Summed billed cost of every billing line attributed to this state, decimal string.

computed_at.description: Latest attribution recompute that produced these rows (RFC 3339). Absent when nothing is attributed to the state.

currency.description: Billing currency when every attributed line uses the same one. Absent when mixed or when nothing is attributed.

line_count.description: Billing lines attributed to the state.

resources.description: Per-resource split of the state total, one entry per matched address.

window_end.description: Latest charge period end (falling back to start) among the state's attributed lines (RFC 3339).

window_start.description: Earliest charge period start among the state's attributed lines (RFC 3339).

state-cost-unsupported.description: Companion view to state-costs: the subset of the latest snapshot's resources that are either unsupported by the pricing engine or recognised-but-unpriced. Used by the UI to surface coverage gaps.

state-cost-unsupported-resource.description: One resource from the latest snapshot that didn't contribute to the totals -- either because the type isn't recognised by the pricing engine (supported=false) or because it's recognised but has no billable line items (no_price=true).

state-costs.description: Latest cost snapshot for a state: top-level totals + coverage counters + the per-resource instance_costs breakdown. Returned by GET /api/v1/states/{state_id}/costs. 404 when the state has never been priced.

calculated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which the snapshot was written.

coverage_percent.description: priced_count / resource_count * 100, or 100 when resource_count is 0.

hourly_cost.description: Snapshot-level total hourly cost (sum over priced resources). Decimal string (not a JSON number) so sub-cent precision is preserved. Absent when no resource in the snapshot is priced.

monthly_cost.description: Snapshot-level total monthly cost (sum over priced resources). Decimal string (not a JSON number) so sub-cent precision is preserved. Absent when no resource in the snapshot is priced.

priced_count.description: Number of resources for which the snapshot contains a non-zero priced result.

resource_count.description: Total resources considered by the snapshot.

source.description: How the numbers were obtained. Currently always "estimate" (pricing-engine quote); a future "actual" source will fold in reconciled cloud-bill data.

supported_count.description: Number of resources whose type is recognised by the pricing engine (may exceed priced_count when some are free/no_price).

triggered_by.description: What caused this snapshot to be created: "state_import", "tx_apply", "actuator_commit", "scheduled", "manual", or "preview".

count.description: Number of fragments the task's result occupies. Fetch each by its zero-based idx; every fragment decodes on its own, and their concatenation in index order is the payload. A result small enough to fit in a single row has a count of 1.

tenant-cost-attribution.description: Attribution coverage for a tenant's actual (FOCUS) spend: billed cost and line counts split into attributed (matched to a managed resource by cloud identifier) / unmanaged (names a real resource outside the graph) / unallocated (nothing to match on), whole-tenant plus per-provider. This is attribution coverage -- what share of the bill we can pin to something -- distinct from the pricing coverage_percent in tenant-costs (which resources the pricing engine can estimate).

attributed_cost.description: Billed cost attributed to managed resources, decimal string.

attributed_count.description: Billing lines attributed to managed resources.

by_provider.description: The same split per cloud provider.

computed_at.description: Latest attribution recompute (RFC 3339). Absent when attribution has never run for this tenant.

coverage_percent.description: attributed_cost / total_cost * 100 -- cost-weighted attribution coverage. 0 when there is no billed cost.

currency.description: Billing currency when every loaded billing line uses the same one. Absent when currencies are mixed (the summed money fields then have no single unit) or when there are no billing lines.

line_count.description: Total billing lines loaded for the tenant.

matcher_version.description: Version of the matching rules that produced the stored attribution. Absent when attribution has never run.

total_cost.description: Total billed cost across all loaded billing lines, decimal string.

unallocated_cost.description: Billed cost with no resource identifier to match on (taxes, support, fees, account-level charges), decimal string.

unallocated_count.description: Billing lines with nothing to match on.

uncomputed_count.description: Billing lines not yet classified -- loaded after the last recompute, or attribution has never run. 0 in steady state.

unmanaged_cost.description: Billed cost naming real resources Stategraph does not manage -- spend outside the graph, decimal string.

unmanaged_count.description: Billing lines naming resources outside the graph.

window_end.description: Latest charge period end (falling back to start for lines without an end) across the loaded billing lines (RFC 3339). Absent when there are no billing lines.

window_start.description: Earliest charge period start across the loaded billing lines (RFC 3339). With window_end, the span the billed totals cover -- needed to compare them against monthly estimates honestly. Absent when there are no billing lines.

tenant-cost-attribution-provider.description: Per-provider attribution split: the tenant-cost-attribution buckets scoped to one cloud provider.

currency.description: Billing currency when every loaded billing line uses the same one. Absent when currencies are mixed (the summed money fields then have no single unit) or when there are no billing lines.

window_end.description: Latest charge period end (falling back to start for lines without an end) across the loaded billing lines (RFC 3339). Absent when there are no billing lines.

window_start.description: Earliest charge period start across the loaded billing lines (RFC 3339). With window_end, the span the billed totals cover -- needed to compare them against monthly estimates honestly. Absent when there are no billing lines.

tenant-cost-history.description: Tenant cost over time, one point per day, oldest-first. Each day sums every state alive that day -- a state contributes its most recent snapshot as of that day, carried across recompute gaps, bounded by the state's create/delete lifecycle.

tenant-cost-history-point.description: Tenant cost on one day of the history series: the date, the tenant total, and -- when ?group_by is given -- the per-group breakdown for that day.

date.description: The day this point covers (ISO 8601 date).

groups.description: Per-group breakdown for this day; populated only when the request set ?group_by (by provider, resource type, or tag value).

hourly_cost.description: Tenant total hourly cost for the day, decimal string.

monthly_cost.description: Tenant total monthly cost for the day, decimal string. Absent when nothing was priced that day.

tenant-cost-state.description: One state's contribution to a tenant cost rollup. A state that has never been priced appears with its identity only and absent cost fields.

calculated_at.description: When the latest snapshot was computed (ISO 8601). Absent when the state has no snapshot.

coverage_percent.description: Absent when the state has no snapshot.

hourly_cost.description: Decimal string. Absent when the state has no snapshot.

monthly_cost.description: The state's latest snapshot total monthly cost, decimal string. Absent when the state has no snapshot.

resource_count.description: Absent when the state has no snapshot.

supported_count.description: Absent when the state has no snapshot.

tenant-cost-tag-keys.description: The Terraform tag keys present across a tenant's currently-priced resources, for populating a "group by tag" selector.

tenant-cost-unmanaged-entry.description: One unmanaged resource the bill names: actual spend Stategraph attributes to no managed resource. Grouped by (resource_id, provider) across the loaded billing window.

billed_cost.description: Summed billed cost of the resource's billing lines, decimal string.

resource_id.description: The cloud identifier exactly as the billing export names it (FOCUS ResourceId).

tenant-costs.description: Current cost rollup for a tenant: totals and coverage across the latest snapshot of every live state, breakdowns by provider / resource type / (when ?tag_key is given) tag value, and a per-state list. Server-computed so the dashboard renders from one call. Soft-deleted states are excluded.

by_provider.description: Cost broken down by cloud provider.

by_tag.description: Cost broken down by the value of the tag key passed in ?tag_key. Empty when ?tag_key is not supplied.

by_type.description: Cost broken down by Terraform resource type.

currency.description: Currency of the snapshots aggregated. Absent when the tenant has no priced state.

hourly_cost.description: Tenant total hourly cost, decimal string. Absent when nothing is priced.

monthly_cost.description: Tenant total monthly cost -- sum over the latest snapshot of each live state -- as a decimal string. Absent when nothing is priced.

priced_count.description: Resources that produced a non-zero priced result.

resource_count.description: Total resources across the tenant's latest snapshots.

supported_count.description: Resources whose type the pricing engine recognises.

tenant-create-request.description: Body of the create-tenant endpoint: the name of the new tenant.

name.description: The new tenant's display name. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed, and what remains must be non-blank, at most 255 characters, and not already in use by another tenant.

tenant-invitation.description: An invitation as the tenant's administrators see it. `status` is computed: an invitation whose `expires_at` has passed reports as `expired` even while its stored state still says `pending`.

created_at.description: When the invitation was first created (UTC, ISO 8601). Unchanged by a reissue.

delivered.description: Whether the most recent send reached the mail provider: `true` delivered, `false` attempted but not delivered, absent when no send has been attempted (for example when email delivery is not configured -- the copyable link is still valid).

email.description: The address the invitation was sent to, and the address the invitee is expected to sign in as.

expires_at.description: When the invitation expires (UTC, ISO 8601). A reissue resets this to a fresh lifetime.

id.description: The invitation's id, used to reissue or revoke it.

invited_by_name.description: Display name of the user who created the invitation.

role.description: The role the invitee receives on acceptance: `member` or `admin`.

send_count.description: How many times the invitation email has been sent. Bounded by the server's per-invitation send budget; a reissue resets it.

status.description: `pending` (live and unaccepted), `accepted`, `revoked`, or `expired`. Reported as `expired` once `expires_at` passes, regardless of the stored state.

tenant-invitations-response.description: A page of a tenant's invitations, newest first, together with the total count and the cursor needed to page.

has_more.description: True when more invitations follow this page; fetch them by passing `next_cursor` as `cursor`.

limit.description: The page size that was applied, after clamping to the server's bounds.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor to pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. Present only when `has_more` is true.

total_count.description: The tenant's total number of invitations, the same on every page (independent of `cursor`).

tenant-member.description: One active member of a tenant as the administration UI lists them: identity, when they joined, and how their capability grant covers this tenant. The `*_scope` fields distinguish a grant scoped exactly to this tenant from one that reaches wider, because a wider grant cannot be edited from here.

admin_scope.description: How the member's admin grant covers this tenant: `none` (not an admin here), `tenant` (scoped exactly to this tenant), or `wider` (reaches beyond it -- installation-wide or a broader pattern). A `wider` grant cannot be changed through the tenant membership endpoints, so the UI disables demote and remove for such a member.

avatar_url.description: URL of the member's avatar, when set.

email.description: The member's email address when one is on file. Absent for a user who has never had an address recorded -- it is nullable and is not re-synced after first sign-in.

joined_at.description: When the user became a member of this tenant (UTC, ISO 8601). Also the key the member list is ordered and paged by.

type.description: The user's account type, e.g. `user`, `api`, or `system`.

users_manage_scope.description: How the member's `users-manage` grant covers this tenant, with the same `none` / `tenant` / `wider` meaning as `admin_scope`.

tenant-member-add-request.description: Body of the add-member endpoint: the existing user to add to this tenant. For someone who has no account yet, send an invitation instead.

user_id.description: The id of an existing user to add as a member of this tenant.

tenant-member-remove-response.description: Confirmation that a member was removed from the tenant.

removed.description: Always true in a success response; the field exists so the result is an explicit object rather than an empty body.

tenant-member-set-role-request.description: Body of the set-role endpoint. Each field is an independent grant toggle: send `true` to grant, `false` to revoke, and omit a field to leave that grant untouched. Tenant-administrator (`admin`) and membership-management (`users-manage`) are separate rights.

can_manage_users.description: Set `true` to grant the right to manage this tenant's membership, `false` to revoke it; omit to leave it unchanged.

tenant_admin.description: Set `true` to grant tenant-administrator rights over this tenant, `false` to revoke them; omit to leave admin unchanged. Revoking your own admin, or the tenant's last administrator, is refused with 409 `LAST_TENANT_ADMIN` / `CANNOT_ACT_ON_SELF`.

tenant-members-response.description: A page of a tenant's active members, oldest membership first, together with the total count and the cursor needed to page.

has_more.description: True when more members follow this page; fetch them by passing `next_cursor` as `cursor`.

limit.description: The page size that was applied, after clamping to the server's bounds.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor to pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. Present only when `has_more` is true.

total_count.description: The tenant's total number of active members, the same on every page (independent of `cursor`).

tenant-resource-types.description: What a tenant's states hold, broken down by resource type. One entry per state and resource type, carrying both how many resources of that type the state declares and how many instances of them are deployed, plus the totals across every entry. `total_instances` is the tenant's full instance count; `total_resources` is not the tenant's full resource count, because a resource type with nothing deployed has no entry and so contributes to neither number.

items.description: One state and one resource type: the resources of that type the state declares, and the instances of them that are deployed. The instance count exceeds the resource count wherever `count` or `for_each` expands one address into several objects.

tenant-security-breakdown-entry.description: Tenant-wide security posture for one day of the history series: the date, the total open findings across the tenant (each live state contributes its most recent completed `current` scan as of that day, carried across re-scan gaps, bounded by state lifecycle), and that day's counts under each breakdown dimension. The most recent entry doubles as the current-posture snapshot.

blast_breakdown.description: Findings bucketed by blast-radius impact relative to the window's largest blast: "low" (< 25% of max), "medium" (25-75%), "high" (> 75%); largest-impact first. Buckets partition findings_total_count. When the window's max blast is 0, all findings fall in "low".

date.description: The day this entry covers (ISO 8601 date).

findings_total_count.description: Total findings across the tenant as of this day.

severity_breakdown.description: Findings bucketed by effective severity. Missing keys default to 0; the buckets partition findings_total_count.

tenant-security-history.description: Tenant-wide security posture over time. Returned by GET /api/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/security/findings/history. `points` is the day-by-day series (oldest-first); the current-posture snapshot is the last point (when `states_scanned` > 0). `states_total`/`states_scanned`/`last_scanned_at` summarise coverage and freshness for the headline cards.

last_scanned_at.description: Most recent completed current scan across the tenant (ISO 8601). Absent when none.

states_scanned.description: Live states with at least one completed current scan.

tenant-update-request.description: Body of the tenant rename endpoint (`PUT /api/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}`). A tenant's only editable attribute is its display name.

name.description: New display name for the tenant. Must be non-blank and at most the server's maximum length; a name already in use by another tenant is rejected with 409 `TENANT_NAME_CONFLICT`.

created_by_name.description: Display name of the user that opened the transaction. Omitted by endpoints that do not load enrichment, and when that user no longer exists.

state_names.description: Names of the states the transaction writes to. Omitted by endpoints that do not load enrichment.

tx-cost-delta.description: Current-vs-planned cost delta for one transaction. `totals` is the tenant-tx-wide summary; `states`, `by_provider`, `by_type` and `by_tag` are the same delta sliced different ways, all derived from the same (current snapshot set, planned snapshot set) pair so the numbers add up consistently. Returned by GET /api/v1/tx/{tx_id}/costs.

by_provider.description: Delta broken down by cloud provider, most-impacting first.

by_tag.description: Delta broken down by each distinct Terraform tag key present on either side. One entry per tag key; each entry carries the per-value rows for that key.

by_type.description: Delta broken down by Terraform resource type, most-impacting first.

states.description: Per-state delta rows for every state the tx touches, including each state's per-resource change list.

tx-cost-resource-delta.description: One resource's cost change within a transaction's per-state delta. Joined by resource address between the state's current snapshot and the tx's planned snapshot. Resources whose cost is identical on both sides are excluded; only added / removed / cost-changed resources appear.

change_kind.description: One of "added" (in planned only), "removed" (in current only), or "changed" (in both with different cost).

delta_monthly_cost.description: Signed. Absent when neither side has a priced monthly cost (e.g. unsupported resource added).

tx-cost-state-delta.description: Per-state contribution to a transaction's cost delta: identity, the state's total cost on each side, the signed delta, and the per-resource change list. `resources` is empty when the tx touches the state but no resource's cost actually changes (e.g. tag-only edits).

tx-cost-status.description: Non-ready response from GET /api/v1/tx/{tx_id}/costs. Today the only emitted status is "computing" (returned with HTTP 202 when the planned-cost preview is still being computed in the background). A tx that has aborted returns HTTP 404 instead: the abort endpoint deletes the planned snapshots, so the delta isn't a meaningful concept after an explicit abandon. Failed dashboard-apply txs keep their planned snapshots and serve 200/202 like a pending tx; commits keep theirs as a preserved-prediction delta.

tx-cost-tag-breakdown-delta.description: Cost delta broken down by the values of one Terraform tag key. `entries` is the per-value list (one row per distinct tag value present on either side, plus an "untagged" bucket for resources lacking the key).

tx-cost-totals-delta.description: Top-level totals + coverage counters for a transaction's cost delta. Each metric carries current / planned / signed-delta triplets; money fields are absent on a side when nothing is priced there, currency is absent in the mixed-currency case (matching Phase 2's totals contract).

currency.description: Currency of the snapshots aggregated. Inherits from the only priced side when one side is empty; agrees on the shared value when both sides are priced; absent only when the two priced sides disagree (mixed-currency case; callers should render the deltas without a single-currency label).

tx-detail.description: The run-detail payload for one transaction: the tx with its list enrichment and the states it touches. The per-resource plan operations and the captured apply output are served separately, paginated, by GET /api/v1/tx/{tx_id}/plan-operations and GET /api/v1/tx/{tx_id}/output.

share_url.description: Signed public share link for this run. Null until the share-token service lands.

state_ids.description: Ids of the states the transaction writes to.

tx-output-chunk.description: One stored chunk of a transaction's apply output.

data.description: The base64 of one fragment of the payload's JSON text, cut between codepoints and outside escape sequences, so a chunk decodes on its own: a fragment of the apply's stdout string literal (the first chunk opens the quote, the last closes it) can be shown before the other chunks are fetched, and wrapped in quotes it parses as a JSON string. The whole payload is the concatenation of the decoded chunks in ascending idx, JSON-parsed. Served as stored, unmasked: tofu's own "(sensitive value)" redaction is all the redaction there is.

idx.description: Zero-based chunk position within the output.

tx-output-chunks.description: One page of a transaction's apply output.

payload.description: What the chunks reassemble to, from the state of the task that ran the apply: apply_stdout when it completed (a JSON string, tofu's stdout), run_failure when it failed (a run-failure record, a refused run included). Absent when no output has been stored yet, i.e. the page is empty.

results.description: Chunk rows in ascending idx. Paginated via Link header (RFC 5988): follow rel="next" for further chunks. Empty when no output has been stored yet (the apply has not run, or is still running), or the transaction predates the tx-to-task link.

skip_data_source_refresh.description: RFD 584. Do not refresh this transaction's data sources. A plan whose configuration has not changed still opens a transaction so a data source whose RESULT moved is reachable; setting this says the caller knows they have not moved and does not want the round trip, so the refresh gate answers the preview immediately.

tx-security-impact.description: Per-transaction security impact: the findings the planned change adds and resolves vs each affected state's latest current scan, computed at plan time, plus the scan/state context shared with the rollup. `findings_added` are present in the planned scan but absent from the current scan; `findings_resolved` are present in the current scan on a re-scanned resource but absent from the planned scan. Returned by GET /api/v1/tx/{tx_id}/security/impact; the severity rollup is at .../impact/summary.

computed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the impact was computed.

cross_boundary_finding_count.description: Number of findings in the delta whose blast or cross-state refs cross a state boundary.

findings_added.description: Findings the planned change introduces (new vs the current scan).

findings_resolved.description: Findings the planned change removes (gone vs the current scan).

scan_ids.description: Ids of the security_scans rows aggregated into this impact -- typically one per state touched by the tx.

source.description: "planned" = computed at plan time from a preview; "commit" = computed post-apply.

states_affected.description: State ids touched by this tx, in the order their scans were aggregated.

tx-security-impact-severity-counts.description: Finding counts bucketed by effective severity. Absent buckets are zero.

tx-security-impact-status.description: Non-ready response from GET /api/v1/tx/{tx_id}/security/impact. Returned with HTTP 202 while the impact computation is still in flight; clients should poll. Today the only emitted status is "computing".

tx-security-impact-summary.description: Per-transaction security impact rollup: added/resolved finding counts bucketed by severity vs each affected state's latest current scan. Returned by GET /api/v1/tx/{tx_id}/security/impact/summary; the detailed finding lists are at .../impact.

computed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the impact was computed.

cross_boundary_finding_count.description: Number of findings in the delta whose blast or cross-state refs cross a state boundary.

scan_ids.description: Ids of the security_scans rows aggregated into this impact -- typically one per state touched by the tx.

source.description: "planned" = computed at plan time from a preview; "commit" = computed post-apply.

states_affected.description: State ids touched by this tx, in the order their scans were aggregated.

filepath.description: Path of the file relative to its owning module directory.

node_id.description: Stringified Sg_node.Id of the file to delete.
Stringified Sg_node.Id of the HCL block to delete.

data.description: AST-encoded HCL block, as produced by Hcl_parser_value_json.Safe.of_ast on a single element.

file.description: Source filename of the HCL block (e.g. "main.tf").

file_refs.description: Per-block file_refs JSON: a map of call-key to resolved file_ref descriptors, or null when the block has no file()-family calls.

module.description: Fully-qualified module address that owns this block. Empty string for the root module.

module_source.description: Raw [source] argument of the enclosing module call. Null for the root module.

ref_hints.description: Module-output ref hints used to bridge dynamic module.X[*].out lookups. Presence (even as []) is authoritative on the server.

tx_log_set_refresh.description: RFD 584. Appended by a plan whose configuration has not changed, in place of the hcl_set/tfvar_set/file_set entries a changed configuration produces. It opens a transaction where the revision-hash comparison would otherwise have short-circuited, so a data source whose RESULT moved is still reachable. It seeds nothing: the subgraph's seeds come from the data source results the refresh discovers, and a state with no data sources makes the transaction a noop.

state_id.description: The state whose data sources are to be refreshed. Echoes the envelope's state_id so the log row names its subject on its own.

data.description: Sg_tf_state_json.Check_results.t with the [objects] field elided. Each object is emitted separately as a [check_result_entry].
One Sg_tf_state_json.Check.t object, tagged with the parent's [config_addr].

object_addr.description: Fully-qualified instance address this check entry pertains to.

data.description: Sg_tf_state_json.Instance.t merged with the resource-scoped fields below. Permits Instance.t fields (schema_version, attributes, dependencies, index_key, status, ...) in addition to those listed.

address.description: Fully-qualified instance address (resource_address + index suffix when keyed).

module.description: Owning module address, when not at the root.

resource_address.description: Fully-qualified address of the owning resource.

sensitive.description: Sensitive flag from the state file. Null when absent.

type.description: Terraform type expression for the output value (arbitrary JSON, as in the state file).

value.description: Output value, copied verbatim from the state file.

module.description: Owning module address, when not at the root.

provider.description: Provider source string from the state, when present.

lineage.description: Stable lineage UUID assigned by Terraform when the state was created.

terraform_version.description: Terraform version that produced the state file (e.g. "1.7.5").

node_id.description: Stringified Sg_node.Id of the tfvar to delete.

tx_log_set_tfvar_ephemeral.description: A tfvar whose value changes every run and changes nothing, such as a per-run authentication token. Matches tfvar_set in shape, but never seeds the subgraph, is never committed to the database, and has its value masked in the MQL interface.

data.description: Expression-encoded value, as produced by Hcl_parser_value_json.Safe.of_expr.

file.description: Source filename the tfvar was loaded from (e.g. "terraform.tfvars").

name.description: Tfvar name (the bare identifier, without the [var.] prefix).

data.description: Expression-encoded value, as produced by Hcl_parser_value_json.Safe.of_expr.

file.description: Source filename the tfvar was loaded from (e.g. "terraform.tfvars").

name.description: Tfvar name (the bare identifier, without the [var.] prefix).

asset_name.description: GCP Cloud Asset Inventory asset name

id.description: Generic resource identifier (ARN for AWS, asset_name for GCP)

is_instance_admin.description: Whether to create the user with the installation-wide admin grant -- an unrestricted admin capability, covering every tenant there is and every tenant there will be. Setting it to true requires the caller to hold that grant already, over and above the capability that reaches this endpoint, because the caller also chooses the new user's password; a caller without it is answered 403 and no user is created. Defaults to false, which creates the user with the installation's default capabilities and no admin grant. A tenant-scoped admin cannot be created here; grant one through the tenant members API afterwards.

The installation-wide admin grant the created user holds, echoing the request. There is no is_tenant_admin counterpart because creation cannot write a tenant-scoped grant: a user is created either with the unrestricted admin capability or with none.

user-detail-response.description: One user's record. capabilities is present when the caller is the user, or the caller holds authority over the user (i.e. if it can edit this user's data). It is absent otherwise.

tenants.description: The tenants the user is a member of, as id and name pairs. Empty when the user belongs to no tenant.

tenants_complete.description: Whether the tenants list holds every membership of the user. False when memberships outside the caller's scope were withheld; the list then holds only the memberships inside that scope. True for the user's own record and whenever the caller reaches every tenant.

is_instance_admin.description: The installation-wide admin grant to leave the user with. True writes an unrestricted admin capability, replacing any tenants allow-list the user held; false removes an unrestricted admin capability and leaves a tenant-scoped one untouched. The value is set, not toggled: the current grant is never read to invert it, so repeating a call changes nothing.
